problems.title: Table 6 cannot be reconciled with its displayed dataset scores
claim: Table 6 compares NMI methods at \(1024\)- and \(2048\)-token KV-cache budgets for Llama-\(3.1\)-8B-Instruct and Phi-\(3.5\)-Mini-3.8B-Instruct. It lists \(16\) dataset scores and an Average for each of \(18\) rows. The following results paragraph describes EHPC as achieving the best average across compression rates Section 5.2, p. 9.
This finding concerns the aggregate comparison actually used to support that interpretation. It is not a claim that an individual score is fabricated or that every qualitative advantage disappears.
analysis: The displayed Llama SnapKV scores at budget \(2048\) sum to \(603.37\), giving the equal-dataset mean \(37.710625\), while Table 6 reports \(35.80\). The EHPC scores at the same budget sum to \(606.72\), giving \(37.92\) rather than \(37.86\). These differences exceed display rounding. An unreported weighting rule is not assumed; individual dataset values are not replaced.
result: This is a supported local finding within the stated source/formulation scope. Its effect on the paper's aggregate experimental results remains unmeasured.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: Make the Average entries consistent with the stated aggregation of the displayed dataset cells, or state the different weighting or aggregation rule explicitly.
problems.impact_rationale: The counterexample limits an interpretation or special case while leaving the central method and reported observations intact; it warrants Minor.

problems.title: Even-width pooling can duplicate a token instead of deleting only
problems.source_location: Sections 3.1–3.2, Eq. (1), PDF p. 4; Appendix D, PDF p. 23 (pooling defaults).
claim: Paraphrase. Section 3.1 defines compression by dropping tokens, and Section 3.2 constructs the compressed prompt from retained tokens in their original order p. 4, Equation 1. The output is therefore intended to be a subsequence of original positions. Appendix D sets average pooling with kernel width \(32\), using observation windows \(16\) for Llama and \(4\) for Phi p. 23.

The active implementation is standard_dis_index in my_baseline/GemFilter/gem_filter_utils.py, lines 92–131. It is called by find_context, which passes the returned indices to the model layer. get_layer_context in my_utils/my_generation.py, lines 9–20, sorts and gathers those indices, then appends the last observation window.
analysis: Stride-one symmetric pooling of \(M\) prefix scores with width \(r\) produces \(M+2\lfloor r/2\rfloor-r+1\) outputs. For even \(r=32\), this is \(M+1\). The extra index \(M\) already belongs to the original suffix. If selected by top-k and then followed by the appended suffix, it occurs twice, so the result is not a deletion-only subsequence.

An explicit valid indexing fixture has \(N=80\), suffix window \(W=16\), prefix length \(M=64\), target budget \(k=48\) and pool width \(r=32\). Use one-dimensional unit queries, with prefix keys zero except key \(63\) equal to \(20\). Its dominant positive attention score contributes to every pooled position from \(48\) through \(64\). All these \(17\) positions belong to the top \(32\), so the out-of-prefix index \(64\) is selected and then appended again with suffix \(64,\ldots,79\). No author routine was executed in this reassessment.
result: This is a supported local finding within the stated source/formulation scope. Its effect on the paper's aggregate experimental results remains unmeasured.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: Before top-k selection, restrict the pooled scores to the original prefix length \(M=N-W\). The selected prefix indices then lie in \(\{0,\ldots,M-1\}\), disjoint from the appended suffix \(\{M,\ldots,N-1\}\); sorting gives exactly \(k\) distinct original positions for the valid budget \(W\leq k\leq N\). This repairs the indexing invariant, not benchmark accuracy.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a demonstrated local release/specification mismatch. Its use in the table-producing runs and any substantial effect on the core scientific conclusion have not been established, so Minor is appropriate.

problems.title: Released NMI timing double-counts prefill and mislabels per-token time
problems.source_location: Section 5.1, PDF pp. 8–9 (EMI); Appendix F, PDF p. 24 (NMI); released my_utils/my_generation.py, lines 147–185 and 226–247.
claim: Appendix F reports separate prefill and decode-per-token speed ratios for NMI, while Section 5.1 has a distinct EMI compression-time comparison pp. 8–9, 24. The following defect is in the released NMI implementation, not a direct reconstruction of the published timing table.

eval/LongBench/pred.py calls my_greedy_generate_config for the compressed-prompt path and stores its returned times fields alongside predictions. Other native-model paths call my_greedy_generate_standard_time. The relevant functions are in my_utils/my_generation.py, lines 147–185 and \(226\)–247.
analysis: Write selection, compressed-prefill and decode intervals as \(C,P,D\). The released latency sums \(C+2P+D\), although the main elapsed interval is \(C+P+D\). Its per-token field is \((P+D)/G\), including prefill, and its time-to-first-token adds a separate post-response generation probe. Those labels do not partition the declared operation. The published timing-table incidence is unestablished.
result: This is a supported local finding within the stated source/formulation scope. Its effect on the paper's aggregate experimental results remains unmeasured.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: Use the main elapsed interval for latency and measure the actual first and last generated-token events. With start \(t_0\), first token \(t_F\), last token \(t_L\) and \(G>1\), define TTFT as \(t_F-t_0\) and TPOT as \((t_L-t_F)/(G-1)\), stating synchronization and overhead conventions. The post-first-token mean is undefined for \(G=1\). This does not reconstruct the published speed table.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a demonstrated local release/specification mismatch. Its use in the table-producing runs and any substantial effect on the core scientific conclusion have not been established, so Minor is appropriate.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: Displayed averaging arithmetic, an even-width indexing invariant and NMI timer labels have bounded counterexamples. These local corrections do not establish loss of the prompt-compression method’s central benefit or a replacement empirical speed/accuracy result; Minor is appropriate.
